key_insight: AI-driven monocular markerless motion capture can accurately quantify the Upper Extremity Reachable Workspace (UERW) from a single camera, making objective biomechanical assessment feasible in routine clinical settings.
problem_solved: Replaces expensive, complex multi-camera/marker-based motion-capture setups with a clinically accessible, single-camera pipeline that objectively measures UERW, lowering barriers to adoption in clinics and rehab settings.
method: Capture monocular video and apply AI pose-estimation to extract 2D/estimated 3D joint keypoints.
Use a biomechanical reconstruction pipeline to compute the 3D reachable workspace and standardized UERW metrics from keypoints.
Validate the monocular MMC outputs against clinical gold-standard measurements (e.g., marker-based systems) using statistical comparisons and error analyses.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to build and deploy lightweight, validated clinical motion-analysis tools that support remote or low-cost assessment, facilitate larger-scale data collection, and accelerate translational research in rehabilitation and biomechanics.
visual_elements: Side-by-side photo: single-camera capture with skeleton overlay vs. marker-based system (illustrates accessibility gains).
3D spherical/polar 'reachable workspace' plot showing area/volume computed from upper-extremity motion.
Pipeline diagram: Video → AI pose estimation → biomechanical reconstruction → UERW metrics → validation plots.
Validation chart (scatter or Bland–Altman) comparing monocular MMC UERW values to gold-standard measurements.
paper_title: Monocular Markerless Motion Capture Enables Quantitative Assessment of Upper Extremity Reachable Workspace
paper_authors: Seth Donahue, J. D. Peiffer, R. Tyler Richardson, Yishan Zhong, Shaun Q. Y. Tan
